=== PMID: 27491313 ===

Title: Catechol-O-methyltransferase Val158Met polymorphism is associated with increased risk of multiple uterine leiomyomas either positive or negative for MED12 exon 2 mutations.

Journal/Date: Journal of clinical pathology (2017)

MeSH Keywords: Adult, Catechol O-Methyltransferase, DNA Mutational Analysis, Exons, Female, Genetic Predisposition to Disease, Genotype, Humans


--- ABSTRACT ---
[AIMS]: To study the possible association of catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT) Val158Met polymorphism with multiple and solitary uterine leiomyomas (ULs) and to check whether the COMT Val/Val genotype is associated with MED12 exon 2 mutations in fibroids.
[METHODS]: The COMT Val158Met allele and genotype frequencies were compared between age-matched women with ULs (n=104) and controls (n=59). Patients with UL were subcategorised by diagnosis of solitary (n=59) or multiple (n=45) fibroids and by the presence of somatic MED12 exon 2 mutations in at least one fibroid (n=32) or in neither fibroid (n=26). The association of COMT Val/Val genotype with the presence of any ULs, solitary/multiple ULs and ULs positive/negative for MED12 exon 2 mutations was evaluated by χ2 tests using a dominant genotype model (G/G vs G/A+A/A) and expressed as ORs and 95% CIs.
[RESULTS]: The COMT Val/Val genotype frequency did not differ between the patients with UL and the controls (28.8% vs 18.6%, p=0.149, OR 1.77; CI 0.81 to 3.86). However, it was significantly higher in the patients who had multiple UL compared with the solitary UL (40% vs 20.3%, p=0.028, OR 2.61; CI 1.09 to 6.24) and to the controls (40% vs 18.6%, p=0.016, OR 2.91; CI 1.20 to 7.06). No association of the COMT Val/Val genotype with UL-specific MED12 exon 2 mutations was found (p=0.662, OR 0.77; CI 0.23 to 2.53).
[CONCLUSIONS]: Women with COMT Val/Val genotype are at high risk of developing multiple uterine fibroids either positive or negative for MED12 exon 2 mutations. These data are important to design new strategies for UL prophylaxis and treatment.

key_findings.finding: The directly relevant primary study is Heinonen et al., J Clin Pathol 2017 (PMID 27491313): 104 women with uterine leiomyomas and 59 age-matched controls; 59 had solitary and 45 had multiple leiomyomas. COMT Val/Val frequency was 28.8% in all leiomyoma patients versus 18.6% in controls (OR 1.77, 95% CI 0.81–3.86, p=0.149), so there was no statistically significant increase in overall leiomyoma risk.

Thus the evidence supports an association with multiplicity rather than with leiomyoma occurrence overall.

key_findings.finding: The MED12 analysis in the 2017 study did not show genotype-specific enrichment: 32 patients had at least one fibroid with a MED12 exon 2 mutation and 26 had neither fibroid mutated; the association of COMT Val/Val with MED12-mutated versus non-mutated leiomyomas was not significant (p=0.662, OR 0.77, 95% CI 0.23–2.53). The authors therefore concluded that the increased risk of multiple leiomyomas applied to both MED12-positive and MED12-negative tumors, with no evidence that the COMT association differed by MED12 status.

source_tools.relevance: Primary-study abstract explicitly giving MED12 subgroup sizes, OR, CI, p value, and conclusion

key_findings.finding: Other primary COMT–leiomyoma studies are inconsistent and generally did not evaluate MED12 status: a 2006 study included 186 women with leiomyomas and 142 without and reported Val/Val associated with approximately 2.5-fold higher risk (95% CI 1.017–6.151, p<0.001); a 2007 NIEHS study included 972 premenopausal women (576 Black, 396 White) and found no association; a 2013 Turkish study included 105 cases and 105 controls and found no overall association (p=0.46), although Met allele frequency was associated with fibroid size (p=0.011, OR 0.50, 95% CI 0.28–0.90); and Chinese case-control studies reported positive associations for rs4680, including OR 2.593 (95% CI 1.546–4.350; n=300 cases/300 controls) and OR 5.675 (95% CI 2.696–11.942; n=800/800). These studies do not establish a MED12-specific effect.

source_tools.relevance: Search results summarizing primary-study sample sizes and effect estimates
PubTator annotations confirming rs4680/Val158Met and leiomyoma associations in the cited primary studies

key_findings.finding: A 2013 meta-analysis of 7 articles/12 case-control studies found a small protective association in a reported dominant comparison (OR 0.84, 95% CI 0.70–0.99, p=0.04), especially in Black populations (OR 0.68, 95% CI 0.48–0.97, p=0.03), while a 2022 meta-analysis including 4,969 leiomyoma cases and 4,934 controls reported a pooled rs4680 association in the opposite direction (OR 0.83, 95% CI 0.71–0.97, p=0.02; model as reported). These pooled results concern overall leiomyoma risk and provide no MED12-stratified evidence.
